summary: Ottawa heads into a busy fall with a budget update, trade talks with the United States and a Bank of Canada rate decision later this month.
body: Parliament returns this week with the economy at the top of the agenda. The federal government is expected to present a fall update on spending and deficits, and opposition parties have signalled they will focus on housing costs and the price of groceries [^1].

Trade remains the biggest outside pressure. Talks with the United States over tariffs on steel, aluminium, autos and lumber are continuing ahead of the scheduled review of the North American trade agreement, and businesses say the uncertainty is delaying investment decisions [^2].

The Bank of Canada makes its next interest rate decision at the end of the month. Inflation is close to its 2 percent target, but unemployment has crept up, which is why some economists expect another small cut while others expect the bank to wait [^3].
differences: Business groups describe the trade talks as close to a deal; union and opposition voices say the main sticking points have not moved.
